options: Compressing several datasets into a single archive file
Splitting one dataset into multiple smaller datasets for parallel processing
Encrypting data from several systems with a single key
Pulling the same nature of data from multiple source systems and correlating it to produce one unified output
Migrating data from an old system to a new one
questions.explanation: Data Fusion is about pulling the same nature of data from multiple source systems to correlate it and produce one unified output.

questions.stem: Which sales channels are given as examples of where data for a particular product can come from in Data Fusion?
options: POS (point of sales), shops and online stores
Payroll, HR and finance systems
Email, calendars and contact lists
Weather feeds, maps and traffic data
Backup servers and archive tapes
questions.explanation: The example lists product data coming from POS, from shops and from online stores, alongside conversations about the product elsewhere.

questions.stem: Apart from sales channels, where else might people be talking about a product in the Data Fusion example?
options: In tax returns and audit reports
In internal database logs
On social media, in seminars and in webinars
In supplier invoices
In warehouse stock counts
questions.explanation: The example notes that people can talk about the product on social media, in seminars and in webinars, and fusing those data elements with sales data is valuable.

questions.stem: Which teams are said to gain valuable information from fusing all the data about a product?
options: Legal and compliance teams
Database administrators
Network engineers
Backup and recovery teams
Sales and marketing teams
questions.explanation: Fusion of the product's data elements can produce valuable information about that product for sales and marketing teams.

questions.stem: How is the term Data Fusion characterised in relation to other data terms?
options: As a brand-new term with no equivalent
As another term that overlaps with many terms already in place
As a term used only in Data Science
As a legal term for data sharing agreements
As an outdated term no longer used
questions.explanation: Data Fusion is introduced as another term overlapping with many other terms already in place.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT named as a data store that can be used for Data Fusion?
options: Data Warehouse
Data Mart
Data Lakehouse
Data Vault / Business Vault
Integration Hub
questions.explanation: Data Warehouse, Data Mart, Data Lake, Data Lakehouse and Data Vault / Business Vault are all named as stores usable for Data Fusion; Integration Hub is not.

questions.stem: What is the intended result of Data Fusion?
options: Several separate reports, one per source system
One unified output
A compressed copy of each source system
A list of duplicate records
A mirror of the source data
questions.explanation: Data Fusion correlates data from multiple sources to produce one unified output.

questions.stem: In Data Fusion, what does pulling the same nature of data mean?
options: Gathering data about the same subject, such as one product, from different source systems
Gathering only data stored in the same file format
Gathering data from a single system at different times
Gathering data that has exactly the same column names
Gathering data of the same size from each system
questions.explanation: The product example shows that data about the same subject is pulled from POS, shops, online stores and social conversations, then correlated.

questions.stem: What is the key activity that Data Fusion performs on the data it pulls from multiple sources?
options: Deleting it after use
Encrypting it at rest
Splitting it by region
Correlating the data elements with each other
Ranking it by file size
questions.explanation: Data Fusion correlates the same nature of data from multiple source systems with each other to produce a unified output.

questions.stem: Which statement about Data Fusion and data stores is correct?
options: Data Fusion can only be achieved in a Data Lake
Data Fusion requires a dedicated store separate from all existing ones
Data Warehouses, Data Marts, Data Lakes, Lakehouses and Data Vaults can all be used for Data Fusion
Data Fusion cannot be done in a Data Mart
Data Fusion replaces the need for a Data Warehouse
questions.explanation: The same fusion can be achieved in a Data Warehouse, Data Mart, Data Lake, Data Lakehouse or Data Vault / Business Vault; all of those stores can be used for Data Fusion.
